summary: The note surveys small business openings in September-October 2023 across cities worldwide, grouping them into trends such as eco-consciousness, technology, wellness, artisanal revival, specialty food, remote education, subscriptions, personalization, fitness, urban farming and co-working. Each global example is paired with a local counterpart to show how entrepreneurs draw on global movements to shape their communities. It concludes that small business owners are shapers of the local economy, reflecting a global heartbeat with a local pulse.
one_line: Overview of 2023 small business trends, pairing global openings in cities like Sydney, Tokyo and Berlin with local counterparts.
key_facts: Amelie Nguyen opened 'Green Future Boutique' in Sydney, Australia on September 12th; it stocks only products made from recycled materials.
'Code & Craft', co-founded by Marcus Johnson, opened in San Francisco on September 20th offering web design, app development and digital marketing for small businesses.
'Hygge Health' launched September 5th in Copenhagen, Denmark, founded by siblings Emma and Lucas Rasmussen, selling all-natural skincare and offering mental health wellness workshops.
'Artisan's Alley', a collective space for local craftspeople, was inaugurated by Mayor Linda Garcia on October 1st on the local Main Street; founder is Pedro Alvarez.
'Taste of Tradition', owned by Fiona Byrne, opened in London on September 15th offering rare cheeses and heritage meats.
'NextGen Tutors', founded by Hiroki Matsuda in Tokyo, opened virtually on October 3rd and connects students with tutors worldwide.
'Monthly Mania', founded by Jasmine Patel, launched September 8th in Toronto, Canada with theme-based monthly boxes for hobbyists.
'Print Your World', co-owned by Dieter Muller, opened October 14th in Berlin, Germany, specializing in 3D-printed accessories customers design themselves.
'Mindful Moves', owned by Soo-Min Park, opened September 7th in Seoul, South Korea, combining fitness with mindfulness practices.
'Cultiva Ciudad', founded by Rodrigo Solis, opened September 25th in Mexico City to teach city dwellers to grow organic produce in limited spaces.
'CoLab Workspaces', founded by Ananya Singh, launched September 17th in Bangalore, India as a co-working space.

Local counterparts named include 'Local Harvest', 'Bright Horizons Tutoring', 'Locale Box', 'ZenFit Studios', and 'Workspace Collective', which opened last month; jeweler Maria Lopez tailors each piece to customers.
